_note: Dynamic crises (scripts/sim/crisis.gd). Each month, while the scenario has pressure_ai, the quarrels of the world are weighed: for a nation `a` and a neighbour (or, between great powers, any nation) `b`, score = hostile * how much b dislikes a ... see score. A pair may quarrel only if the demander's side (with allies and guarantors) has gate.min_odds of the other side's strength; a scenario claim is pressed only from gate.claim_min_tension. The best pair at or above gate.min_score opens a crisis: `a` makes a demand of `b` (a province claim, a border province, an indemnity, or the withdrawal of border armies) with a deadline. `b` yields, refuses (a gets a casus belli with the demand as its goal, and the AI may declare war at once), mobilizes (if a cannot win it backs down) or appeals to the powers. A third nation may mediate or back a side. The AI answers for itself after think_days; the player is asked at once if the crisis is theirs.

claim.title: {a} presses its claim on {b}
claim.text: {a} demands {what} from {b}, which it says is rightfully its own, and gives {b} until {date} to answer.

border.title: {a} demands land from {b}
border.text: {a} demands {what} from {b} and gives it until {date} to answer.

indemnity.title: {a} demands reparations from {b}
indemnity.text: {a} claims it was wronged and demands {what} from {b}. It gives {b} until {date} to answer.

disarm.title: {a} demands {b} withdraw from the border
disarm.text: {a} will not stand {b}'s armies on its frontier and demands {what}. It gives {b} until {date} to answer.
